title: Probe retirement and dashboard consolidation plan
body:
Summary:

This doc lays out a pragmatic, low-friction plan to retire legacy probes and consolidate the proliferation of dashboards created during Q3–Q4 2024. Goals: reduce maintenance burden, lower query cost, remove noisy alerts, and preserve investigation fidelity for high-impact failure modes. The approach balances automated migration, short-lived feature flags, and operator validation windows.

Why now:
- Query and dashboard costs have grown 38% year-over-year; many widgets duplicate signals across tenants.
- Several probes (http_request.lat_raw, gen.kv_hit_rate_v0) were instrumented as part of experiments and never standardized.
- Oncall churn from false-positive alerting remains a common hire blocker for our SRE rotation.

High-level strategy:
1) Inventory and classification: tag probes as canonical / experimental / deprecated.
2) Map consumer surfaces: dashboards, alerts, SLOs, notebook queries, automation (runbooks).
3) Create a migration plan per-probe: rename -> alias -> cutover -> retire.
4) Dashboard consolidation: merge panels into composite microdashboards per-journey and prune extraneous widgets.
5) Trace anchoring: make sure traces continue to capture session_id + request_path + model_variant for multi-hop resolutions.
6) Communication & validation windows with owners and oncall.

Inventory & classification process (owner: Diego Ramirez)
- Run probe inventory script (linked Confluence doc) to produce CSV with columns: probe_name, metric_type, producers, consumers, estimated query_cost_per_month, last_used (dashboard / alert / notebook).
- Classify:
  - canonical: core platform metrics we maintain (e.g., inference.request.count, kv_cache.eviction_rate).
  - experimental: short-lived signals created for A/B experiments or perf debugging; flag for 90-day auto-delete.
  - deprecated: replaced by canonical equivalents, scheduled for retirement after migration.
- Deliverable: triaged CSV and a one-line rationale per deprecated probe.

Mapping consumers (owner: Priya Singh)
- For each deprecated probe identify: dashboards (grafana panel id), alerts (alertmanager rule id), notebooks and CI jobs.
- Rank consumer impact: high (SLO/alert), medium (dashboards used in incident review), low (ad-hoc notebooks).
- Update linked_artifacts with found ids in the CSV output.

Migration pattern (per-probe)
1) Create alias metric: emit deprecated_probe_name as deprecated_probe_name.deprec_alias and simultaneously emit canonical metric for the same events (dual-write) for 14 days.
2) Update dashboards/alerts to read canonical metric with a migration flag (feature-flagged queries) so operator workflows can toggle between legacy and new source.
3) Monitor differences: create a small smoke dashboard that shows a per-probe delta % between legacy and canonical for the 14-day window. Acceptable divergence: <3% for volumetric counters; <0.5% absolute for key ratios.
4) After validation window, flip queries to canonical. Keep legacy alias as read-only for 30 days.
5) Schedule deletion of legacy probe instrumentation and related storage after 60 days unless tied to a SLO rollback.

Example renames (illustrative)
- http_request.lat_raw -> inference.request.lat_p50 (canonical)
- gen.kv_hit_rate_v0 -> kv_cache.hit_rate (canonical)
- session.token_flow_steps -> request.step_count (canonical)

Tracing guidance during cutover (owner: Oliver Park)
- Maintain trace anchors: session_id, request_id, model_variant, route_version. These must be present on both legacy and canonical spans to enable joinability.
- Sampling: temporarily increase sampling to 100% for traces that touch both legacy and canonical metrics for the 14-day validation window (bounded to 24h/day and capped at 10k traces/day).
- Tagging: add migration_tag=\"probe-migration-<probe>\" to traces emitted during the dual-write phase to ease queries.
- Post-cutover: return sampling to baseline with target-based adaptive sampling for error and SLA-related traces.

Dashboard consolidation plan (owner: Maya Chen)
- Audit existing dashboards and group by user journey: onboarding, inference-serving, batch-indexing, embeddings.
- For each group, create a microdashboard with 8–12 panels: SLO anchors + top 5 investigation signals + capacity/cost panel.
- Consolidate any panels with overlapping queries by replacing multiple panels with a single multi-stat panel.
- Remove panels that are seldom used (last_viewed > 120 days) unless flagged for archival.
- Introduce a lightweight dashboard metadata file in repo (YAML) that records owner, purpose, panel_cost_estimate. PRs required for dash changes.

Alert rationalization
- Reviews by alert owner: keep only alerts that protect SLOs or are necessary for safety.
- Convert high-noise alerts to pageless Slack notifications with runbook links and quieter thresholds for 2-week trial.
- Implement score-based alerting for signals with weak numeric correlation to user impact (score = weighted-sum of error, latency, customer-visible-fraction).

Rollback & safety net
- Canaries: apply the migration to a single non-critical tenant first (dev-dedicated) for 48–72 hours.
- Feature flags: all query rewrites must be behind ff toggles so panels can be switched back quickly.
- Short-term retention: keep legacy metrics accessible for 60 days post-cutover in a read-only archive.
- Runbooks updated: link each migrated dashboard/alert to an updated runbook and a line listing the migration tag to search traces.

Timeline (Q1 2025 sprint-aligned)
- Week 1: run inventory, classify probes, create triage CSV.
- Week 2: map consumers and create migration backlog tickets (OBS-34xx).
- Weeks 3–4: implement dual-write alias in telemetry agent; create smoke dashboards.
- Weeks 5–6: validate differences, iterate on instrumentation if divergence > thresholds.
- Week 7: roll consolidated dashboards to staging; oncall review.
- Week 8: cutover for non-critical tenants; Week 10: full cutover & begin retirement window.

Operational checklist (to complete per-probe and per-dashboard)
- [ ] Owner assigned and notified in ticket
- [ ] Dual-write implemented and smoke dashboard created
- [ ] Trace migration_tag and sampling increase active
- [ ] Divergence < threshold for 14-day window
- [ ] Dashboard queries updated behind feature flag
- [ ] Oncall signoff and runbook updated
- [ ] Legacy metric retired and storage decommissioned after retention window

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Decide global divergence thresholds for ratio vs. count metrics (proposal: 3% volumetric, 0.5% ratio).
- Confirmation on cost budget for trace sampling bump (finance/observability).
- Agreement on archival retention policy for retired metrics (default 60 days).

Next steps:
- Diego and Priya to publish triaged CSV to Confluence by 2025-02-17.
- Maya to propose 3 pilot dashboards for consolidation by 2025-02-21 (dev dashboards selected).
- Oliver to land trace tagging PR (gh #418) and enable sampling cap for pilot tenants by 2025-02-24.

Appendix: quick query examples (pseudocode)
- Smoke divergence panel:
  SELECT time_bucket(1m, ts) AS t,
         sum(legacy_count) AS legacy, sum(canonical_count) AS canonical,
         100.0 * (sum(legacy_count)-sum(canonical_count))/nullif(sum(canonical_count),0) AS pct_delta
  FROM telemetry.dual_write_probe
  WHERE probe = 'http_request.lat_raw'
  GROUP BY t
  ORDER BY t

- Trace search for migration traces:
  service:inference AND tags.migration_tag:\"probe-migration-http_request.lat_raw\"

Notes: keep this doc light and actionable. We should avoid a big-bang rip-out; prioritize reversible, observable steps so engineers and SREs can verify parity before any deletions.
